claims.text: The deviation is made out on the booked baseline. The GPS trace for TRP-02837 records trace_distance_km of 13.2 against a booked optimal of 10.0 km, an excess of 3.2 km — 32.0% of the optimal route and 3.2 km in absolute terms. Both POL-RD-01 gates pass (excess greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km), and the platform's own derived deviation block scores the status as 'established'. Nothing in POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12 has been shown to reduce that excess on this record.

The governing distance figure is the trace, not the rounded trip_record convenience copy: POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km govern where the two disagree, and forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test. The trace carries 104 fixes at a 10-second sample interval over 100.0% coverage with an empty gaps array, and the derived excess on it is 3.2 km / 32.00%, so the threshold test is run on a clean measurement rather than a rounded field.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and discharges it. The trip identifier TRP-02837 is the same on trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the pickup timestamp matches between the trace's first fix (2026-08-16T17:00:12+08:00) and the trip_record's started_at (2026-08-16T17:00:12+08:00); and limb (b) is satisfied by the threshold excess measured above. The burden therefore shifts to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific exculpatory clause; a general assertion that the rider moved a pin, with no artifact tying that to the measured excess, does not discharge it.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 and needs no independent corroboration. Limb (a) does not fire: max_gap_sec is 0.0 and the gaps array is empty. Limb (c) does not fire: the sampling interval is 10.0 seconds, far under the 30-second ceiling. Limb (b) does not fire: there are no straight-line jumps to speak of across 104 consecutive fixes. The admissibility pre-pass accordingly rates the artifact COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0, so no confidence cap attaches under POL-GEN-02 and the rider's measurement is not required to be corroborated from the POL-RD-07(ii) list.

No traffic advisory covers this trip, and I disclose the impairment of the artifact I cite for that: EV-ADVIS-02837-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT at BLOCKING severity, and carries no payload. There is therefore no advisory naming a road or segment the optimal route traverses, no validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle reaching any such segment, and nothing to match a corridor departure and rejoin. POL-RD-03 cannot exonerate any part of the excess on this bundle, and an external-traffic explanation from either side carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13.

The only rider instruction in the chat log is the single message sent at 17:03:32, 'actually can you drop me at the other building, i changed the pin'. It names no road and no place that can be acted on, and chat_message.waypoint_hint is null — the platform resolved no coordinate from it. Under POL-RD-04(c) that instruction is too vague to ground an exoneration, and because waypoint_hint is null the 200 m corroboration test cannot be run at all, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable on the record; read instead as an uncorroborated instruction, POL-RD-14 reaches the same result. Either way, the instruction excludes no distance from the measured excess.

The driver's explanation is that the rider moved the drop-off pin, and the trip_record does show dropoff_amended_at at 17:04:12 with a re-quote of 13.4 km. But both the original and the amended drop-off carry the identical label 'Blk 112 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4' (the original marked '(original pin)'), so what the record actually shows is the pin being refined at the one building the rider had already booked to, not a relocation to a different destination. A pin refinement inside the same labelled address does not account for a re-quote 3.4 km longer than the 10.0 km optimal stored at booking. It is the driver, on whom POL-RD-08 puts the burden, who must show that a rider-caused relocation explains the measured excess before POL-RD-05 displaces the booked baseline for the whole trip, and no artifact in the bundle does that. The rider asks the tribunal to state both figures — booked optimal 10.0 km and amended 13.4 km — on the face of the ruling.

If the deviation stands, the refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 and not discretionary. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 10.0 optimal km + 0.28 x 14.0 optimal min) x 1.0 surge_multiplier read from fare_breakdown + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 fixed surcharges + 0 waiting_time_fee - 0 promo_discount = 16.02. Refund = charged_total 19.32 - 16.02 = 3.30, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and is 17.08% of charged_total, below the 90% share that would convert it to a FULL_REFUND. The fare artifact's own derived block independently records the payable figure as 3.30.

The present payment state matters to the outcome: the fare_breakdown records payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so on this rider-filed dispute a NO_ACTION would leave the rider still carrying the disputed distance and time charge rather than returning it. A rider win here requires an outcome that takes the excess distance and time charge off the rider, which on the arithmetic above is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 3.30 — the rider does not ask for the whole contested amount, because the policy arithmetic does not produce it.

The drop-off point on this trip was amended after booking: trip_record.dropoff_amended_at is non-null at 2026-08-16T17:04:12 and sits alongside a stored amended_optimal_distance_km of 13.4 km and amended_optimal_duration_min of 18.5 min. Under POL-RD-05 the threshold test must therefore be re-run against the optimal route between the AMENDED endpoints, and what governs is that stored 13.4 km re-quote - not the 10.0 km booked optimal the rider's claim measures against. Because the amended optimal is present on the record, POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged and no substitute figure need be derived.

Re-applying POL-RD-01 against the amended endpoints, the governing actual distance is the trace figure of 13.2 km (gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs over the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km) and the governing optimal is the amended 13.4 km. The excess is 13.2 - 13.4 = -0.2 km: the driver drove slightly LESS than the platform's own amended optimal route. No deviation survives the recomputation, so under POL-RD-05 the outcome is NO_ACTION.

The amendment is not the driver's invention. It is corroborated by the chat log, where the rider wrote at 17:03:32 'actually can you drop me at the other building, i changed the pin', and by the trip record, which shows the dropoff amended 40 seconds later at 17:04:12. On the record this is a rider-moved pin of exactly the kind POL-RD-05 addresses, so the baseline moves with it.

The trace is clean and unimpaired: 104 fixes at a 10 second sample interval spanning 17 minutes 10 seconds, coverage_pct 100.0, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec 0.0. None of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires, so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes, it is the governing measurement of actual distance under POL-RD-01, and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises.

POL-RD-05 also excludes the distance driven before the amendment: the trip started at 17:00:12 and the pin was amended at 17:04:12, so roughly the first four minutes of driving cannot be counted as excess against the driver on any view of the booked route.

Even if the rider's preferred baseline were used, the excess those fields yield is 3.2 km and 32.0%: that clears the establishment gates (0.8 km and 20%) but fails both materiality gates (8.0 km and 50%). No MATERIAL deviation is recorded, so the POL-RD-06 profile check and its FULL_REFUND uplift are not triggered on this trip at all.

In any event the driver_profile carries no repeat-deviation pattern under POL-RD-06: deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the required 3, and 1 divided by completed_trips_90d of 237 is 0.0042, far below the 0.05 ratio, with completed_trips_90d comfortably above the 40-trip minimum. Both citable counters point the same way and neither supports a conduct finding.

The fare ledger gives the rider nothing separate to recover: it bills 13.2 km, the same distance the trace records, with zero ERP or toll lines and no airport surcharge line. There is therefore no unmatched or phantom charge line to correct under POL-RD-09(4), and nothing for POL-RD-10(8) to escalate.

The only deficient artifact in the bundle is the traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-02837-01, which is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - no advisory covers this corridor in this window. I disclose that impairment. It costs the driver nothing: the driver asserts no external traffic cause and does not invoke POL-RD-03, so the absence cannot be turned against him, and because no party cites it as an advisory covering this trip, POL-RD-13 confirms that this is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction engaging POL-RD-10(5).

There is no escalation trigger on identifiers or timestamps: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry TRP-02837, and the trace's first fix 17:00:12 and last fix 17:17:22 match the recorded start and completion to the second. POL-RD-10(2) and POL-RD-10(4) do not fire, and the timestamps do not run backwards anywhere on the record.

On a rider-filed dispute that the evidence does not support, the correct outcome is NO_ACTION: fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0, so leaving the present state untouched leaves the $19.32 fare standing and returns nothing to the rider. NO_ACTION is not a restoration of the charge - it is simply the present state, which here favours the driver.

ruling.explanation: Addressed to both parties. This is a rider-filed route-deviation dispute over trip TRP-02837 and the SGD 19.32 charged fare, and the rider's claim is not upheld. NO_ACTION: the fare stands and no refund issues. The rider's arithmetic is right on its own terms — the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02837) records 13.2 km against the 10.0 km optimal stored at booking (EV-TRIP-02837), an excess of 3.2 km / 32.0% that clears both POL-RD-01 establishment gates, and the trace governs over the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km. The trace is clean (104 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0), so POL-RD-07 does not impair it and POL-RD-10(3) does not fire. The claim fails because the booking baseline moved. POL-RD-05 applies: the trip_record shows the drop-off amended after booking, dropoff_amended_at 2026-08-16T17:04:12, and carries the stored amended_optimal_distance_km of 13.4 km (amended_optimal_duration_min 18.5). The chat log (EV-CHAT-02837) corroborates it — the rider wrote at 17:03:32 'actually can you drop me at the other building, i changed the pin' — and the driver's statement says the same. POL-RD-05 requires the threshold test to be re-run against the amended endpoints on that stored re-quote, and bars the Judge from deriving a substitute figure. Re-run: 13.2 - 13.4 = -0.2 km. No deviation survives the recomputation, and POL-RD-05 directs NO_ACTION. The rider's answer — that both pins carry the label 'Blk 112 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4' and this was therefore a pin refinement rather than a relocation — is rejected: the amended pin is a different coordinate (1.3295, 103.871 against the original 1.3267, 103.8733), the platform recorded the amendment and produced a stored re-quote, and the clause keys on the recorded amendment, not on the label. The driver's separate POL-RD-04 point is also answered: the rider's message names no place and chat_message.waypoint_hint is null, so the 200 m corroboration test cannot be run and POL-RD-04 excludes nothing; the excess is removed by POL-RD-05 instead. Remaining points, answered together: POL-RD-03 is unavailable and no party asserted an external traffic cause — the missing advisory EV-ADVIS-02837-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT, issued by a party citing no advisory covering this trip) is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation, and it carries no fact. POL-RD-06 is not engaged: there is no MATERIAL deviation (3.2 km / 32% is under both material gates) and no trail under the clause's citable counters (deviation_flags_90d = 1; 1/237 = 0.004), the driver profile's other fields being context only under POL-GEN-01, so no conduct referral arises. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02837) carries no phantom gantry or surcharge line, so POL-RD-09 gives no correction; the trip identifiers and the trace's first and last fixes match the trip_record across the board, so POL-RD-10(2) and (4) do not fire, and no refund approaches the ceiling. Figures used: trace distance 13.2 km (EV-GPS-02837); booked optimal 10.0 km and amended optimal 13.4 km (EV-TRIP-02837); charged total SGD 19.32 (EV-FARE-02837). Confidence 0.9, above the 0.70 floor. This is a provisional ruling; either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.

This ruling is addressed to both parties. In short: the rider changed the drop-off point during the trip, so the longer distance travelled is the distance the rider asked for, and the claim is not supported. The SGD 19.32 already charged stands and the SGD 4.50 disputed is not returned.

WHAT THE RECORD SHOWS. On 16 Aug 2026 the rider booked Blk 55 Lengkok Bahru to Blk 112 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4 (EV-TRIP-02837). The platform's booking-time route estimate (optimal_distance_km) was 10.0 km. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02837: 104 fixes, 10 s interval, 100% coverage, empty gaps) measures the distance driven at 13.2 km, and the fare ledger (EV-FARE-02837) bills the same 13.2 km for a charged_total of 19.32. On the booked baseline the excess would be 3.2 km / 32%, which would clear the POL-RD-01 gates (0.8 km and 20%).

WHY THE BOOKED BASELINE IS NOT THE GOVERNING ONE. The trip_record shows the drop-off point was amended after booking: dropoff_amended_at is 2026-08-16T17:04:12, and the stored re-quote amended_optimal_distance_km of 13.4 km (duration 18.5 min) sits with it. The rider's own in-app message at 17:03:32 (EV-CHAT-02837) reads 'actually can you drop me at the other building, i changed the pin'. POL-RD-05 therefore applies and directs the POL-RD-01 test to be re-run against the optimal route between the amended endpoints. POL-RD-05 makes that a stored field that must be used and not re-derived, and it is present, so no substitute figure is invented and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged. Re-run: actual 13.2 km (the trace governs over the rounded trip_record copy) minus amended optimal 13.4 km = -0.2 km. The driver drove slightly less than the platform's own amended optimal. No deviation survives the recomputation, and POL-RD-05 provides that the outcome is then NO_ACTION.

THE RIDER'S ARGUMENTS, ANSWERED. (a) The rider argues the pin was only 'refined' inside the same building label, so the driver must prove a relocation explains the excess. I reject this: POL-RD-05 keys on the trip_record showing the drop-off amended after booking, which it does, and the rider's own message says they changed the pin to 'the other building'. The clause does not require the label to change, and it was the rider who asked for the change. (b) The rider's establishment claim (3.2 km / 32% on the booked baseline) is correct as far as it goes but is displaced by POL-RD-05. (c) The rider's POL-RD-02 arithmetic (charged 19.32 less recomputed 16.02 = 3.30) is correct as arithmetic, but POL-RD-02 only runs where a deviation is established and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it. POL-RD-05 excuses it, so the 3.30 is never reached. (d) I accept that POL-RD-04 is unavailable here: the message names no road or place and chat_message.waypoint_hint is null, so the 200 m corroboration test cannot be run. That does not help the rider, because POL-RD-05 is a separate clause and applies on the trip_record alone. (e) I accept the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) (max_gap_sec 0.0, 10 s sampling, no jumps), so no POL-RD-10(3) corroboration is required.

OTHER CHECKS. No POL-RD-06 pattern arises: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 (below 3) and 1/237 completed_trips_90d = 0.004 (below 0.05), and no MATERIAL deviation is recorded, so there is no conduct referral and no FULL_REFUND uplift. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02837-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; I name it and it changes nothing, because neither party asserts an external traffic cause and no advisory is invoked under POL-RD-03, so this is a gap in the bundle, not a contradictory invocation. The fare ledger carries no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge line, so there is no phantom charge to correct under POL-RD-09(4) and no POL-RD-10(8) escalation. Trip identifiers (TRP-02837) and timestamps agree across EV-TRIP-02837, EV-GPS-02837 and EV-FARE-02837, so POL-RD-10(2) and (4) do not fire, and no other POL-RD-10 trigger is met. The fare is METERED (quoted_fare_sgd null), so POL-RD-11 does not apply.

OUTCOME. Under POL-GEN-03 the ruling is NO_ACTION: fare_breakdown.payment_status stays CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd stays 0.00. No refund and no driver compensation is due, and there is no clause-mandated referral. Confidence 0.90, capped by the weight 1.0 of the artifacts carrying the deciding facts (EV-TRIP-02837 and EV-GPS-02837, with EV-CHAT-02837 at 1.0 corroborating the amendment). The monetary effect is nil, below the POL-GEN-05 threshold. This is a provisional ruling; either party may appeal once under POL-GEN-04.

To the rider and the driver: the ruling is NO_ACTION. The SGD 19.32 fare stands and nothing is refunded.

Why. On this trip the drop-off point was changed after booking. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02837, weight 1.0) shows dropoff_amended_at at 17:04:12, i.e. during the trip, and stores the re-quoted route to that amended point as 13.4 km (trip_record.amended_optimal_distance_km). The rider's own in-app message at 17:03:32 (EV-CHAT-02837, weight 1.0) — 'actually can you drop me at the other building, i changed the pin' — and the moved pin coordinates (about 400 m from the original pin) confirm the change. POL-RD-05 therefore applies and requires the deviation test to be re-run against the amended route.

The figures. Booked optimal 10.0 km (trip_record.optimal_distance_km). Amended optimal 13.4 km. Actual distance driven 13.2 km (gps_trace.trace_distance_km; where the trace and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree, POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern). Charged total SGD 19.32. Re-running POL-RD-01 on the amended baseline: 13.2 − 13.4 = −0.2 km, so there is no excess at all — the driver drove essentially the route the platform itself computed to the amended destination. No deviation is established, and POL-RD-02 (the fare recomputation the rider relies on for a SGD 3.30 refund) does not run.

The rider's arguments. (1) Your point that both pins carry the label 'Blk 112 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4' and that this was only a refinement of the pin is rejected: POL-RD-05 is triggered by the record showing the drop-off was amended, the coordinates and your own message show a change, and the clause fixes the baseline at the stored amended optimal and expressly forbids the tribunal from re-deriving a substitute figure. (2) Your point that chat_message.waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04 cannot be corroborated, is correct, and POL-RD-14 reaches the same result — but POL-RD-04 is not how the baseline moves here; POL-RD-05 is. (3) Your SGD 3.30 arithmetic is right as arithmetic but does not run once the baseline moves.

The driver's other points. No repeat-deviation pattern exists (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d = 1, below 3, and 1 divided by 237 completed trips = 0.004, below 0.05), so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02837, weight 1.0) bills 13.2 km with no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge line, so there is no phantom charge to correct under POL-RD-09(4).

The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02837-01 is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT). It carries no fact and no weight. Because no party invoked it and none asserts an external traffic cause, its absence is a gap in the bundle, not an escalation trigger under POL-RD-10(5) (POL-RD-13).

No escalation trigger fires: the GPS trace is clean for policy purposes (EV-GPS-02837, weight 1.0 — 100% coverage, 10-second sampling, an empty gaps array, max_gap_sec 0.0, so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) do not fire); the identifiers all read TRP-02837; the timestamps agree; and confidence is above the 0.70 floor. The monetary effect is nil and so below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold.

Either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04 within 30 days.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this is the route-deviation dispute over trip TRP-02837, on which the rider was charged SGD 19.32.

What the evidence shows. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02837, weight 1.0, COMPLETE — 104 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, empty gaps array) records the distance driven as 13.2 km. The route estimate stored at booking was 10.0 km, and that is the figure the rider's complaint measures against; on that comparison the excess is 3.2 km / 32.0%, which clears both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (over 20% and over 0.8 km). The rider is right that the trace figure governs over the rounded trip_record copy.

Why that comparison is not the one that decides the case. The trip record shows the drop-off point was amended after booking: trip_record.dropoff_amended_at is 2026-08-16T17:04:12, and the record carries the platform's re-quoted optimal for the amended destination, amended_optimal_distance_km = 13.4 km, with amended_optimal_duration_min = 18.5. POL-RD-05 therefore requires the threshold test to be re-run against the AMENDED endpoints, and it requires the stored 13.4 km figure to be used — the policy expressly forbids me to re-derive a substitute. Re-run: 13.2 km (trace) less 13.4 km (amended optimal) = minus 0.2 km. No excess survives; the driver drove slightly less than the platform's own optimal route to the amended destination. POL-RD-05 states that where no deviation survives the recomputation, the outcome is NO_ACTION. The rider's POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 claims (deviation established at 3.2 km; refund of 19.32 - 16.02 = 3.30) are rejected for that reason, and no ERP or surcharge line needs correcting, so POL-RD-09(4) produces nothing.

The rider's message and why POL-RD-04 does not rescue the rider. The chat log's single message, sent 17:03:32, reads 'actually can you drop me at the other building, i changed the pin', and chat_message.waypoint_hint is null. The message names no road or actable place, and with no waypoint coordinate the 200 m corroboration test cannot be run, so POL-RD-04 exonerates nothing (and POL-RD-14, on an uncorroborated instruction, reaches the same non-result). The amendment itself is dealt with under POL-RD-05, which does not depend on a waypoint hint. The rider's argument that the message is too vague to ground an exoneration is accepted, but it does not undo the recorded pin change.

The 'same label' point. I accept the observation that both the original pin ('Blk 112 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4 (original pin)') and the amended pin ('Blk 112 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4') carry the same building name, and that a pin move of roughly 0.4 km sits oddly beside a re-quote 3.4 km longer than the booked optimal. But POL-RD-05 is triggered by the record showing the drop-off was amended after booking and it directs me to the stored amended optimal; it gives me no licence to fall back to the 10.0 km booked figure or to invent a different re-quote on the strength of the labels. I have noted the point as an open question below.

Trace integrity. Limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 do not fire: max_gap_sec is 0.0 with no gaps, the sampling interval is 10.0 seconds (well under the 30-second ceiling) and there are no straight-line jumps above 500 m. The pre-pass rates the trace COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so no confidence cap attaches under POL-GEN-02 and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02837-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; neither party asserts an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the absence neither exonerates the driver nor escalates the case (POL-RD-13).

Other checks. No repeat-deviation pattern: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 (below 3) and 1 divided by completed_trips_90d of 237 is 0.004 (below 0.05), so POL-RD-06 gives no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral; the excess (32.0%) is in any case below both materiality gates (50% and 8.0 km). The trip identifiers all read TRP-02837 and the timestamps (first fix and started_at 17:00:12; last fix and ended_at 17:17:22) agree to the second, so no POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires. No clause produces a referral on these facts.

Outcome. NO_ACTION. The claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state stands: fare_breakdown.payment_status remains CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd remains 0.00, so the SGD 19.32 fare stays in place. The monetary effect is SGD 0.00, below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold in POL-GEN-05.

The burden therefore shifts to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific exculpatory clause; a general assertion that the rider moved a pin, with no artifact tying that to the measured excess, does not discharge it.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 and needs no independent corroboration. Limb (a) does not fire: max_gap_sec is 0.0 and the gaps array is empty. No traffic advisory covers this trip, and I disclose the impairment of the artifact I cite for that: EV-ADVIS-02837-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT at BLOCKING severity, and carries no payload.
